acceptance_signals: A strict agentgov.documentation-archive-plan 1.0 schema and dependency-free planner classify dated development-log files against an explicit through-date without using the current clock.

The planner treats archiving as logical index inclusion only, preserves every existing log path, and produces an exact candidate index with target path, create-or-update action, prior and candidate digests, and candidate Markdown.

The command agentgov plan documentation-archive PATH --through YYYY-MM-DD renders terminal or JSON output and performs no repository write in success, warning, failure, advisory, or not-applicable scenarios.
Deterministic filename, date, title, path, and digest findings remain separate from the advisory human decision about whether the candidate index is useful or should ever be applied.
Fixture-based tests cover passing, warning, failing, advisory, not-applicable, stable ordering, multiple same-day records, existing-index update, and filesystem no-mutation behavior.

README, a dedicated guide, STATUS, the dated development log, and protecting documentation tests describe the development-preview command and its denied Git, publication, release, deployment, deletion, rename, and write authority.
Focused tests, the baseline unittest suite, task and repository checks, and git diff --check pass; any pre-existing changes from the separately completed migration task remain separately attributed.

decision.rationale: On 2026-08-14 Documentation Archive and Index Plan v1 delivered the admitted read-only CLI, strict 1.0 contract, deterministic logical eligibility, exact candidate output, protecting fixtures, and user documentation. The real-repository no-mutation check, 47 focused tests, complete 821-test suite with 2 skips, task and repository checks, JSON parsing, and git diff --check passed. A distinct native current-Agent self-review found no correction-required requirement, architecture, scope, implementation, security, data, or authority drift. This paused task authorizes no index write, apply path, schedule, reminder, source-log mutation, Git action, publication, release, deployment, or follow-on implementation.

requirement.summary: Implement Documentation Archive and Index Plan v1 as a read-only development-preview CLI and strict contract: scan repository dated development logs through an explicit date, classify logical index eligibility without moving files, render an exact candidate docs/development-log/INDEX.md plan in terminal or JSON, separate deterministic findings from advisory human usefulness judgment, and provide no apply, schedule, Git, publication, release, deployment, deletion, rename, or external-write capability.

items: A planner could accidentally imply that eligible files may be moved or deleted, breaking stable evidence paths.
Using the host clock would make output and tests non-deterministic.
Loose filename or path handling could include traversal, symlink escapes, or unrelated Markdown files.
Candidate index ordering or title extraction could drift across platforms or duplicate same-day records.
The dirty working tree could blur attribution between this task and the separately completed migration task unless paths and evidence remain explicit.
Reviewed assumption: Logical archive eligibility means inclusion in a generated index candidate, never moving or renaming a dated log.
Reviewed assumption: An explicit through-date is required so planning remains deterministic and independent of the host clock.
Reviewed assumption: The canonical index target is docs/development-log/INDEX.md, but this slice only renders its candidate content and never creates or updates it.
Reviewed assumption: A dated Markdown record uses a strict YYYY-MM-DD.md or YYYY-MM-DD-descriptor.md filename and one first-level title; future or non-dated files are not applicable.

Reviewed assumption: README and the dedicated guide are the affected user surfaces for this advanced development-preview command; Quickstart, public HTML, localized pages, release metadata, and workflows remain unchanged because the ten-minute adoption journey and release identity do not change.

Reviewed assumption: The working tree contains separately completed, uncommitted Historical Documentation Migration v1 changes; this task neither replaces their admission nor authorizes Git operations.
Reviewed unknown: Whether users will find a logical weekly archive index useful is not established until later product-owner review.
Reviewed unknown: Any future apply mode, scheduled reminder, or index publication workflow remains undecided and requires separate admission.

title: Implement documentation archive and index plan v1
